study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized cortical thickness asymmetry in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Schizophrenia

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Bayesian Linear Regression was used to establish normative ranges for cortical thickness asymmetry index, controlling for age, sex, Euler number, and scanner. Ten-fold cross-validation was employed to evaluate model generalization.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Subsequently, we used Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021). The training set consisted of 4904 healthy individuals (54.85% female, age range: 6-95 years) which established a normative range for AI, considering an individual's age, sex, Euler number, and scanner.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was the cortical thickness Asymmetry Index (AI), calculated as (LH - RH) / ((LH + RH) / 2) for both whole brain and 160 regional parcels. Positive AI values reflect leftward asymmetry (LH > RH).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We then computed the whole brain hemispheric Asymmetry Index (AI) for cortical thickness for each subject (n) as follows: AI_n = (LH_n - RH_n) / ((LH_n + RH_n) / 2)
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Echave2024.pdf.md: Methods / Cortical thickness hemispheric Asymmetry Index

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Four explanatory variables were used in the normative model: age (linear term, range 6-95 years), sex, Euler number (as a proxy for FreeSurfer surface quality), and scanner (to account for multi-site data from 20 different scan sites).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The training set consisted of 4904 healthy individuals (54.85% female, age range: 6-95 years) which established a normative range for AI, considering an individual's age, sex, Euler number, and scanner.
